transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… my eating has been off for a while. Some nights I just skip dinner, and I’ve lost some weight without really trying. Other nights I’ll just have crackers or cereal because cooking for myself feels… kind of pointless. It’s been going on for months, so I figured I should come in.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I don’t know… maybe a little. I wouldn’t say I’m crying all the time or anything. Just kind of low, I guess.
Are you trying to lose weight?

No… not really. I’m not trying to. I just haven’t had much appetite, and some nights I skip dinner or just eat cereal or crackers because making food feels like too much. The weight loss kind of just happened.
Are you worried about gaining weight?

No… I’m not worried about gaining weight. It’s more that I just haven’t had much appetite. Some nights I skip dinner, or I just pick at cereal or crackers because cooking feels kind of pointless. That’s why the weight loss worried me a little, I guess.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah… I guess so. I still do some of the things, like water the garden or go to book club, but it just feels kind of flat. Sometimes I leave early, or I don’t really start at all.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
I don’t know… maybe a little at times. I wouldn’t say I’m completely hopeless. It’s more like things feel hard to look forward to right now.
How long have you been feeling this low?
Since the divorce was finalized… so, about a year and seven months, I guess. It’s been there in some form since then.
Did these feelings start because of the divorce?
I think so… it really started around when the divorce was finalized. That was about a year and seven months ago.
Do you feel your distress since the divorce has been more intense than you would normally expect for something like that?
I’m not really sure how to measure that. It felt… pretty heavy to me, but I don’t know what’s “normal” for that.
Have there been at least two weeks when you felt down or depressed nearly every day?
Yes… I mean, it’s been pretty much going on since the divorce was finalized. About a year and seven months now.
Before the divorce, had you ever gone through another period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most days?
I don’t really know. I mean… I can’t remember anything like that clearly before the divorce.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Sometimes, yes… not that I have a plan to hurt myself. But I’ll catch myself thinking it might be a relief not to wake up. And that scares me. I know if a client said that to me, I’d take it seriously.
For the past two years, have you felt this low on most days?
Not the full two years, no. It’s been since the divorce was finalized… about a year and seven months.
Do these low feelings come up even when you’re not thinking about the divorce?
I’m not sure. I mean… the divorce is usually somewhere in the background. I haven’t really separated it out like that.
Do you feel down most days even when the divorce isn’t on your mind?
I… I don’t really know. I haven’t paid close enough attention to separate it that way. It just sort of feels there, I guess.
Do you feel down most days?
I think so… most days, yeah. It’s hard to say exactly, but it feels like it’s there more often than not.
When something unrelated to the divorce is going well, do you still feel down?
I don’t know… I guess sometimes things can be fine on the outside and I still don’t feel much different. I haven’t really tracked it that closely.
Do you find yourself preoccupied with the divorce much of the time?
Yeah… I do. I replay it more than I probably should. I keep thinking I must’ve failed at something basic in the marriage, even though I know it’s not that simple.
Have you been feeling guilty a lot lately?
Yeah… I guess I have. I keep going back over the marriage and thinking I must’ve failed at something basic. I know it’s probably more complicated than that, but… it still feels that way sometimes.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… a bit. At work, during case reviews, I’ll read the same note over and over and it just doesn’t stick. And even small decisions—like which call to return first, or what to get for dinner—can take me longer than they should. It’s… embarrassing.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began in clear temporal relation to the divorce, a qualifying psychosocial stressor, and include persistent low mood, anhedonia, poor appetite with weight loss, guilt/preoccupation about the divorce, passive death wishes, and impaired concentration. Although depressive symptoms are clinically significant and have lasted beyond 6 months, the interview repeatedly links the syndrome to the stressor and does not establish prior independent depressive episodes or a recurrent course. Eating-disorder psychopathology and primary anxiety disorder were not supported.
